must_fix.title: Nested dialogs: Escape closes every open dialog and the focus trap gets stuck on the inner dialog's first element
must_fix.evidence: src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx:86-97 adds one document keydown listener per open dialog and does not track which is topmost. Probe (outer Dialog with a button that opens an inner Dialog containing buttons i1, i2, i3; click it, press Tab twice, press Escape once) printed: 'focused on inner open: i1', 'after Tab: i1', 'after 2nd Tab: i1', 'dialogs open after one Escape: []'. Tab cannot move inside the inner dialog, and one Escape closes both dialogs. No test covers nested dialogs; Dialog.test.tsx:323 only renders two sibling dialogs to check their ids.

nits: Tabs: a controlled value that matches no tab leaves every tab at tabindex=-1 (probe printed ['-1','-1']), so the tablist cannot be reached by keyboard; fall back to the first enabled tab for tabindex.
Combobox: ArrowDown on a closed popup with a selected value activates the first option rather than the selected one.
Combobox: hovering an option does not update the active option.
Combobox: the role=status 'No results' element is added together with its text, so some screen readers will not announce it; a status element that is always rendered is more reliable.
Dialog focus trap ignores contenteditable, summary, controls inside a disabled fieldset, and positive tabindex order.
Tab does not respect defaultPrevented from a consumer onClick, while TabList and Combobox respect it for onKeyDown.

Dialog with description="" renders an empty

that aria-describedby points to.
Duplicate option values cause a React duplicate-key warning; nothing guards against or documents this.

report:
Not mergeable yet. There is one bug to fix: the Dialog breaks when one dialog is opened from inside another. `pnpm test` passes (3 files, 80 tests) and `pnpm typecheck` is clean. The README matches the code everywhere I checked, the exports are right, and there are no stray files. Most edge cases behave correctly: - **Tabs:** nested tablists, values with special characters, a disabled `defaultValue`. - **Combobox:** Escape inside a Dialog closes only the popup (the dialog's `onOpenChange` was never called). - **Dialog:** focus returns to the opener even under `StrictMode`. **Must fix: Escape and the focus trap fail with nested dialogs.** Each open dialog adds its own `keydown` listener to `document` (`src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx:86-97`). Every listener fires, and nothing tracks which dialog is on top. I opened an inner Dialog from a button inside an outer Dialog, then pressed Tab twice and Escape once: ``` focused on inner open: i1 after Tab: i1 after 2nd Tab: i1 dialogs open after one Escape: [] ``` - **Focus trap:** Tab can't move past the inner dialog's first button. The outer dialog moves focus into itself first, and the inner dialog then pulls it back to its first item. - **Escape:** one press closes both dialogs instead of just the top one. The usual fix is a stack of open dialogs, where only the topmost one handles Escape and Tab. It needs a regression test. The existing tests (`src/Dialog/Dialog.test.tsx:323`) only render two dialogs side by side to check their ids. **Nits (not blocking):** - **Tabs, unknown value:** a controlled `value` that matches no tab leaves every tab at `tabindex=-1`, so keyboard users can't reach the tablist. I saw `['-1','-1']` with `value="zzz"`. - **Combobox opening:** ArrowDown on a closed popup with a value already selected highlights the first option, not the selected one. - **Combobox mouse hover:** hovering doesn't update the active option. - **"No results" announcement:** the `role="status"` element is added together with its text, so some screen readers won't announce it. A status element that is always rendered would be more reliable. - **Focus trap gaps:** it ignores `contenteditable`, `summary`, controls inside a disabled `fieldset`, and positive `tabindex` order. - **Tab click:** `Tab` ignores `defaultPrevented` from a consumer `onClick`, while `TabList` and `Combobox` both respect it for `onKeyDown`. - **Empty description:** `description=""` renders an empty `

` that `aria-describedby` points to. - **Duplicate option values:** these cause a React duplicate-key warning; nothing stops or documents them.
